rationale: The Chief Justice is likely to keep the opinion narrow—upholding the MRT as a permissible attribution of entity-level realized earnings while reserving broader questions about taxing pure unrealized appreciation—so he is the most probable author. Thomas is very likely to write a lone originalist dissent grounded in Macomber and a shareholder-level realization requirement, with some chance of concurrences (especially from Gorsuch/Kavanaugh/Alito) to emphasize limiting principles and avoid implications for wealth taxes.
